## Para. 6.1

## SECTION I – GENERAL

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] 1.1 This Practice Direction supplements Part 54. It applies to Planning Court claims and appeals to the Planning Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] 1.2 In this Practice Direction “planning statutory review” means a claim for statutory review under—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] (a)section 287 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] (b)section 288 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] (c)section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] (d)section 22 of the Planning (Hazardous Substances) Act 1990; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] (e)section 113 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] 1.3 In this Practice Direction “appeal to the Planning Court” means an appeal under section 289 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 or under section 65 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION I – GENERAL] 1.4 In this Practice Direction “nationally significant infrastructure project challenge” means a claim brought within sections 13 or 118 of the Pl.anning Act 2008

## SECTION II – HOW TO START A PLANNING COURT CLAIM

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION II – HOW TO START A PLANNING COURT CLAIM] 2.1 Planning Court claims must be issued or lodged in the Administrative Court Office of the High Court in accordance with Practice Direction 54C. ## 2.2 The form must be marked the “Planning Court”. ## SECTION III – CATEGORISATION OF PLANNING COURT CLAIMS

## 3.1 Planning Court claims may be categorised as “significant” by the Planning Liaison Judge. ## 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (a)relate to commercial, residential, or other developments which have significant economic impact either at a local level or beyond their immediate locality;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (b)raise important points of law;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (c)generate significant public interest;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (d)by virtue of the volume or nature of technical material, are best dealt with by judges with significant experience of handling such matters; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (e) concern a nationally significant infrastructure project challenge. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] 3.3 A party wishing to make representations in respect of the categorisation of a Planning Court claim must do so in writing, on issuing the claim or lodging an acknowledgment of service as appropriate. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] 3.4 The target timescales for the hearing of significant Planning Court claims, which the parties should prepare to meet, are as follows, subject to the overriding objective of the interests of justice—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (a)applications for permission to apply for judicial review or planning statutory review are to be determined within three weeks of the expiry of the time limit for filing of the acknowledgment of service;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (b)oral renewals of applications for permission to apply for judicial review or planning statutory review are to be heard within one month of receipt of request for renewal;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (c)applications for permission under section 289 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 are to be determined within one month of issue;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (d)planning statutory reviews are to be heard within six months of issue; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] (e)judicial reviews are to be heard within ten weeks of the expiry of the period for the submission of detailed grounds by the defendant or any other party as provided in Rule 54.14. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] 3.5 The Planning Court may make case management directions, including a direction to any party intending to contest the claim to file and serve a summary of his grounds for doing so. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 3.2 Significant Planning Court claims include claims which—] 3.6 Notwithstanding the categorisation under paragraph 3.1 of a Planning Court claim as significant or otherwise, the Planning Liaison Judge may direct the expedition of any Planning Court claim if he considers it necessary to deal with the case justly. ## Nationally significant infrastructure project challenges

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Nationally significant infrastructure project challenges] 3.7 The Planning Court will consider any disputed question of permission in nationally  significant infrastructure project challenges at an oral permission hearing only. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Nationally significant infrastructure project challenges] 3.8 Where the Planning Court grants permission in a nationally significant  infrastructure project challenge, the court may give directions about the future  management of the claim immediately or convene a case management conference on an application or of its own initiative

## SECTION IV – PROCEDURE IN CLAIMS FOR PLANNING STATUTORY REVIEW

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION IV – PROCEDURE IN CLAIMS FOR PLANNING STATUTORY REVIEW] 4.1 The Part 8 procedure must be used in a claim for planning statutory review. Part 8 applies with the modifications set out in this Section. ## Claim form

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] 4.2 A Part 8 claim form must be used and must be filed at the Administrative Court within the time limited by the statutory provisions set out in paragraph 1.2. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] 4.3 In addition to the matters set out in rule 8.2 (contents of the claim form) the claimant must also state–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (a)the name and address of any person that the claimant considers must be served in accordance with paragraph 4.1;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (b)that the claimant is requesting permission to proceed with a claim for planning statutory review;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (Permission is required to apply for planning statutory review under the provisions listed in paragraph 1.2(a) to (e) of this Practice Direction.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (c)a detailed statement of the claimant’s grounds for bringing the claim for planning statutory review;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (d)  a statement of the facts relied on;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (e)any application for directions; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (f)the remedy being claimed (including any interim remedy). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Claim form] (Part 25 sets out how to apply for an interim remedy.)

## 4.4 The claim form must be accompanied by the following documents–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.4 The claim form must be accompanied by the following documents–] (a)any written evidence in support of the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.4 The claim form must be accompanied by the following documents–] (b)  a copy of any decision, order, relevant document or action that the claimant seeks to have quashed;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.4 The claim form must be accompanied by the following documents–] (c)copies of any documents on which the claimant proposes to rely;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.4 The claim form must be accompanied by the following documents–] (d)copies of any relevant statutory material; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.4 The claim form must be accompanied by the following documents–] (e)a list of essential documents for advance reading by the court (with page references to the passages relied on). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.4 The claim form must be accompanied by the following documents–] 4.5 Where it is not possible to file all the above documents, the claimant must indicate which documents have not been filed and the reasons why they are not currently available. ## Bundle of documents at permission stage

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Bundle of documents at permission stage] 4.6 The claimant must file one paginated and indexed bundle containing all the documents referred to in paragraphs 4.3 to 4.5. ## 4.7 Attention is drawn to rules 8.5(1) and 8.5(7). ## Service of the claim form

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Service of the claim form] 4.8 The claim form must be served on the appropriate Minister or government department and, where different, on the person indicated in the following table:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Service of the claim form] If the application is brought under— 1. section 287 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990; or 2. section 113 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004. | The authority who prepared the relevant document. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Service of the claim form] If the application relates to any decision or order, or any action on the part of a Minister of the Crown to which— 1. section 288 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 applies; or 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies. | a. The authority directly concerned with the decision, order or action; or b. if that authority is the claimant, on every person who would, if he were aggrieved by the decision, order, relevant document or action, be entitled to apply to the High Court under section 288 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 or section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 as the case may be. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Service of the claim form] If the application relates to any decision on the part of a Minister of the Crown to which section 22 of the Planning (Hazardous Substances) Act 1990 applies. | a. The hazardous substance authority who made the decision on the application to which the proceedings relate; or b. if that authority is the claimant, on every person who would, if he were aggrieved by the decision, be entitled to apply to the High Court under section 22 of the Planning (Hazardous Substances) Act 1990. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Service of the claim form] If the application is brought under—

## 1. section 287 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990; or

## 2. section 113 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 113 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.] The authority who prepared the relevant document. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 113 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.] If the application relates to any decision or order, or any action on the part of a Minister of the Crown to which—

## 1. section 288 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 applies; or

## 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] a. The authority directly concerned with the decision, order or action; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] b. if that authority is the claimant, on every person who would, if he were aggrieved by the decision, order, relevant document or action, be entitled to apply to the High Court under section 288 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 or section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 as the case may be. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] If the application relates to any decision on the part of a Minister of the Crown to which section 22 of the Planning (Hazardous Substances) Act 1990 applies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] a. The hazardous substance authority who made the decision on the application to which the proceedings relate; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] b. if that authority is the claimant, on every person who would, if he were aggrieved by the decision, be entitled to apply to the High Court under section 22 of the Planning (Hazardous Substances) Act 1990. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] 4.9 In paragraph 4.8 “the appropriate Minister or government department” means the Minister of the Crown of the government department—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] (a)by whom the decision or order was or may be made;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] (b)on whose part the action in question was or may be taken. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] 4.10 Except for the court’s order granting or refusing permission and the reasons for making its order, the Administrative Court will not serve documents and service must be effected by the parties. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 2. section 63 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 applies.] 4.11 The claim form must be served within the time limited by the relevant enactment for making a claim for planning statutory review set out in paragraph 1.2. ## Acknowledgment of service

## 4.12 Rules 8.3(1) and 8.3(2) do not apply to a claim for planning statutory review. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.12 Rules 8.3(1) and 8.3(2) do not apply to a claim for planning statutory review.] 4.13 Any person served with the claim form who wishes to take part in the planning statutory review must file an acknowledgment of service using the relevant form. ## 4.14 Any acknowledgment of service must be—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.14 Any acknowledgment of service must be—] (a)filed not more than 21 days after service of the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.14 Any acknowledgment of service must be—] (b)served on—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.14 Any acknowledgment of service must be—] (i)the claimant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.14 Any acknowledgment of service must be—] (ii)any other person named in the claim form, as soon as practicable and, in any event, not later than 7 days after it is filed. ## 4.15 The time limits under paragraph 4.14 may not be extended by agreement between the parties. ## 4.16 The acknowledgment of service—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.16 The acknowledgment of service—] (a)must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.16 The acknowledgment of service—] (i)where the person filing it intends to contest the claim, set out a summary of his grounds for doing so;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.16 The acknowledgment of service—] (ii)state the name and address of any person the person filing it considers should be served in accordance with paragraph 4.8; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.16 The acknowledgment of service—] (iii)comply with rule 10.5; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.16 The acknowledgment of service—] (b)may include or be accompanied by an application for directions. ## 4.17 Rule 10.3(2) does not apply. ## 4.18 The provisions of Part 15 (defence and reply) do not apply. ## Rule 54.8A—Reply to Acknowledgement of Service

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Rule 54.8A—Reply to Acknowledgement of Service] 4.19 (1) A Reply should be filed only if necessary for the purpose of the court’s decision to grant permission to apply for judicial review, for example, where a discrete issue not addressed in the Claim Form is raised in the Acknowledgement of Service. A Reply is not the occasion to rehearse matters already referred to in the Claim Form. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Rule 54.8A—Reply to Acknowledgement of Service] (2) A Reply shall be as concise as possible and shall not exceed 5 pages. The court may grant permission to exceed the 5-page limit. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Rule 54.8A—Reply to Acknowledgement of Service] 4.20 If a Reply is filed unnecessarily, the court may make any order it considers appropriate, whether as to costs or otherwise.
